content.title: About
content.content: Shrimp teriyaki is a seafood dish where shrimp are quickly stir‑fried in a teriyaki sauce made from soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger. The result is a sweet‑salty flavor with a hint of spice and a tender texture. It can be served on its own or used as a topping for rice, noodles or salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Teriyaki originates from Japan and was traditionally used to glaze fish and meat.
Shrimp are one of the fastest‑growing marine resources, though sustainable harvesting is essential.
Teriyaki sauce comes in light and dark versions; the dark version contains more sugar and caramelizes longer.
In Japan, shrimp teriyaki is often served over rice and garnished with sesame seeds and green onions.
The dish is popular in Asian‑fusion cuisine and appears on many fast‑food menus.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Shrimp provide complete protein needed for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many meat dishes, shrimp contain very little saturated fat.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium supports immune function and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Heart‑friendly omega‑3s
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids in shrimp help lower triglyceride levels.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Soy‑based teriyaki sauce can be high in sodium and may contain added MSG, which some avoid.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Improperly sourced shrimp may contain mercury or cadmium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot shrimp teriyaki over rice, noodles, or mixed vegetables. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, sliced green onions or a squeeze of lime for extra brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked shrimp teriyaki in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
